Hi Asha — thanks for the quick turnaround and for attaching the W-9. A few items so we can avoid payment delays: 

1) 1099 treatment
- If Redwood is paying the US entity directly (payments go to Xylon US bank account), our AP practice is to issue a Form 1099 to the recipient of record (the entity receiving payment) when they meet IRS thresholds. So, yes — the US subsidiary would be the 1099 recipient provided invoices are paid to that entity.

2) Required docs to complete onboarding
- Completed W-9 (we have the signed copy you sent)
- EIN confirmation (IRS CP 147 or a bank letter showing EIN) — we need one form of EIN evidence before we release the first invoice.
- If the invoice is issued by the UK parent but paid to the US subsidiary, we need either:
  • a signed intercompany agreement with billing instructions, or
  • a short attestation from the parent confirming that the US subsidiary is the remittance beneficiary and outlining invoice ownership.

3) International parent tax form
- If the parent is the actual payee on any invoices or will receive payments from Redwood, we would need a W-8BEN-E for the parent. If the parent will not receive Redwood payments and the US subsidiary will be the payee, the parent’s W-8 is optional for our records (but helpful for audit trails).

Next steps for you: 
- Please upload EIN confirmation (PDF or bank letter) to the vendor portal link: https://app.redwood.company/vendor-onboard/4721
- Confirm which legal entity will be the payee on Redwood invoices going forward (US subsidiary vs UK parent) and attach the intercompany notice or signed agreement.

I’m CC’ing Marissa from Vendor Ops to help track the onboarding checklist; she’ll confirm once AP has the EIN evidence and can schedule the payment release. I’ll flag this for a no-hold release once we have the EIN confirmation.

Attachment referenced: redwood_remit_instructions.pdf (application/pdf)
